context: Request: the full set of the firm's Capital Markets offerings that used a 180-day lock-up, with the documents showing each lock-up. Rubric: 1010-00002 (Arbor IPO) and 1037-00001 (Solstice ADS IPO), each with its form-of-lock-up-agreement, plus precision. Withdrawn or proposed IPO drafts (1008-00002, 1015-00001, 1032-00003) and the Penterra secondary 1018-00001 (90-day lock-up; its earlier IPO had 180 days) are outside the set.

runs.failure_point: It never opened one qualifying matter's lock-up form, which its own file-name search had listed, and its answer counted withdrawn and draft offerings as qualifying.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.why: The form of lock-up agreement of one qualifying matter appeared in its own path search at [17], but when choosing what to read it opened only that matter's underwriting agreement, and the answer cites a lock-up analysis memo instead.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The screening review named the matter as having only an underwriting agreement read with no follow-up confirming its lock-up; the agent moved on to another scan.

other_errors.why: The answer asserts five matters as qualifying, including a withdrawn offering and two proposed or draft offerings whose documents it had read as unexecuted (evidence seen at [31]-[47]).
other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) The screening review and the check review both named the draft and proposed matters as possibly not qualifying; the check stage only relabelled their status.

divergence: Mixed (T2 passes; T0, T1 fail). All three runs reached the same candidates through path searches and text-extraction scans, screened them, and first wrote a five-matter answer that counted withdrawn and draft offerings. They split at the check stages, where the critic's reviews differed. In T2 the check review recommended leading with the two completed offerings and labelling the other three as reference-only; the agent did so and passed. In T0 the check review flagged that the draft matters were still counted, and the agent finished without changing the list; T0 had also never opened one qualifying matter's lock-up form, which its screening review had flagged. In T1 the write review suggested that a later secondary-offering matter's earlier offering might qualify; the agent added it, removed it after the next review called it a different deal, and re-added it after a further review called the removal narrowing.
